name: Cuban Sandwiches

cookwares.name: panini press or 10-inch cast iron skillet or cast iron griddle

ingredients.name: sections Cuban bread, split open horizontally

instructions.primary_message: Preheat a panini press or a large cast iron skillet or griddle over medium heat. Lay bread, open side up, on a work surface and spread the bottom and top halves with mustard. Layer bottom and top halves with Swiss cheese. Working only on bottom halves, layer on all of the pickles, ham, roast pork, and salami (if using). Close sandwiches, pressing gently.

Butter top and bottom of panini press and press sandwiches with moderate pressure until crisp on both sides, about 8 minutes. If using a cast iron skillet or griddle, melt half of butter in pan and add sandwiches. Use a second pan to press on them as the first side crisps. When crisp, flip sandwiches, add remaining butter, swirl to coat, and continue cooking while pressing until crisp on both sides, about 10 minutes total. Slice sandwiches in half diagonally and serve immediately.

schema_metadata.keywords: cheese, Cuban, cuban sandwich, easy, ham, panini, pork, quick, sandwich

description: Three glorious meats pressed with cheese, pickles, and mustard until toasty and warm.
notes:
Optional or for serving: 115 g sliced Genoa salami (optional; see note)

Notes: Cuban bread is a soft white bread made with lard. Look for it in Latin bakeries or groceries. If unavailable, use any not-too-crusty, soft white rolls, preferably with some lard or fat baked into them. Salami is a traditional ingredient in Tampa-style Cuban sandwiches, but can be omitted.
author: J. Kenji López-Alt
